text: Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called the "reservoir," which processes input data. The weights between the input and reservoir, as well as the reservoir's self-connections, are typically fixed and trained offline. Only the readout weights connecting the reservoir to the output layer are trained online using a simple linear regression. Reservoirs are trained implicitly during the random weight initialization process, focusing on capturing the dynamics of the input data.
